verdict: real, known: scala/bug#12121 (LB6 / retronym/scala#535 for the set and map addAll cells)
reran: cmd.sh on w3-int reproduces actual.txt exactly; w3-base and the 2.13.18 library jar (classes compiled by scalac 2.13.18) print the same 11 lines. The matrix TSV has 173 WRONG, 28 EXC, 7 HANG, 222 CME, 780 ok as stated; I did not re-run the matrix.
user_impact: Code that feeds a mutable set, map or buffer a lazy transformation of itself: s ++= s.view.map(f), m --= m.keysIterator.map(parent), buf.prependAll(buf.view.reverse). Uncommon, but it compiles without a warning and the result is silently wrong, or for UnrolledBuffer never returns. For sets, only mapped sources go wrong in subtractAll; a plain or filtered view or iterator of the receiver (s --= s.iterator.filter(p), the shape people do write) gives the right result on every Scala set in the matrix.
fixability: design question: the one open on scala/bug#12121 and on #535, whether a lazy source that reads the receiver is snapshotted (one copy for non-strict arguments), detected and rejected (ConcurrentModificationException, possible only where a mutation count exists), or documented as unsupported. Once decided, the buffers are clear cut: widen #538 (any source that is not an immutable or array-backed collection, not only eq) and #548 (addAll, IndexedBuffer.patchInPlace, subtractAll). Behaviour-only; no binary cost.
regression: no (same on 2.13.18; the upstream ticket dates from 2020)
links: GA1: same root cause on ArrayDeque and UnrolledBuffer, a subset of this matrix; this is the primary. LB5 (#534), LB6 (#535), LM2 (#548), LM3 (#538): earlier cells of the same family. GC6: also re-entrancy, but a different mechanism (cached node), kept separate.
note: One finding with GA1, and this is the one to keep: its matrix contains every GA1 cell (ArrayDeque, Queue, Stack, UnrolledBuffer rows) plus sets and maps. It is not new: it is scala/bug#12121, where subtractAll and patchInPlace are already named in the comments, so the title 'open class' is fair but 'prior' should cite the ticket. What the earlier drafts cover: retronym/scala#534 makes ArrayBuffer.insertAll/prependAll copy a possible proxy before shifting (addAll of a view still throws ConcurrentModificationException, which is fail-fast and not counted). #548 does the same for ArrayDeque.insertAll and for patchInPlace at index 0; it leaves ArrayDeque.addAll (own override that appends while reading; wrong for a reversed view), IndexedBuffer.patchInPlace with from > 0 and replaced > 0 (the PR text says so; 8 wrong cells each for ArrayDeque, Queue, Stack), and subtractAll (Shrinkable's default; IndexOutOfBoundsException or wrong). #538 clones only when the source is the UnrolledBuffer itself (eq), so every view or iterator of it is still wrong in insertAll, prependAll, patchInPlace and subtractAll and addAll does not terminate. #535 is tests only (label no-fix) for addAll on HashSet, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, LinkedHashMap, TreeMap; it changes no behaviour, and does not mention HashMap, CollisionProofHashMap, LongMap, AnyRefMap, the java.util wrappers, or subtractAll on any set or map. ArrayBuffer.flatMapInPlace is a different mechanism (IndexedBuffer.flatMapInPlace stores the function's results, clears, then reads them) and does not belong with a rule about arguments; the finding excludes mapInPlace/filterInPlace callbacks that read the receiver but includes this one. It deserves its own small pull request (materialise each result as it is produced; ListBuffer already behaves that way).
